questions.q: I find new ideas more interesting than familiar ones.
I enjoy thinking about abstract concepts.
I keep appointments and rarely run late.
I finish what I start, even when it gets dull.
I feel energised by spending time with strangers.
I prefer a loud party to a quiet evening.
I try to keep the peace, even at some cost.
I trust people until they give me reason not to.
I worry about things I can't control.
Small setbacks throw off my whole day.
I stick with what I know works rather than experiment.
I leave things to the last minute more often than not.
A full day alone recharges me more than a night out.
I'd rather win the argument than smooth things over.
It takes a lot to rattle me.
I go looking for music, films or books I know nothing about.
I have little patience for questions with no practical use.
I keep my things in order without having to think about it.
My plans tend to fall apart in the details.
I start conversations with people I have just met.
In a group I say less than most people there.
I give people the benefit of the doubt when a story doesn't add up.
I decide quickly whether someone is worth my time.
I replay conversations afterwards, looking for what I got wrong.
I sleep fine the night before something big.
Markets, left to themselves, distribute fairly.
Essential services belong in public hands, not markets.
Some speech is harmful enough to restrict.
The state should keep out of private life.
My country should help others before its own poor.
Borders should be more open than they are now.
Climate action is worth real economic cost.
Green rules should hold even when jobs are on the line.
New technology, on balance, makes life better.
Some technologies should be slowed down on purpose.
Strong leaders matter more than strong institutions.
The system is rigged against ordinary people.
Lower taxes matter more than more public services.
More surveillance is a fair price for more safety.
My country should put its own people first.
The dangers of climate change are exaggerated.
Progress means building first and fixing problems as they come.
Experts and institutions usually get it right.
People mostly end up where their own effort puts them.
The gap between rich and poor is the biggest problem we have.
Order in the streets matters more than the right to protest.
Adults should be free to harm themselves if they choose.
Immigration has made my country better.
We should fix problems at home before problems abroad.
I would pay noticeably more for energy to cut emissions faster.
Environmental rules are already strict enough.
I would rather live with the risks of new technology than miss what it brings.
New tools should prove they are safe before anyone can use them.
Most politicians are in it for themselves.
The people running things mostly know what they are doing.
Future generations will live better than ours.
Most of what's changing right now is change for the better.
What I owe my family weighs more than what I owe strangers.
I'd give up real comfort to help a stranger.
Pleasure needs no justification.
Obligations come before enjoyment.
Suffering can give life meaning, not just pain.
A hard life spent on something big beats an easy one.
There are objective right answers in ethics.
Some things are wrong in every era and every culture.
Beauty matters as much as truth.
A beautiful thing needs no other use.
The world is mostly getting worse.
A stranger's suffering moves me as much as a neighbour's.
Enjoying myself is a good enough reason to do something.
A calm, happy life beats a hard, important one.
Right and wrong depend on the culture you're standing in.
Whether something works matters more than how it looks.
I expect my own life ten years from now to be better than it is today.
The problems ahead of us are bigger than anything we have solved.
A life saved far away counts the same as one saved here.
Charity should start with the people around you.
I plan my week around things I will enjoy.
I feel uneasy resting while work is unfinished.
The best parts of my life came out of something difficult.
I would trade a smaller life for a more peaceful one.
Some acts would be wrong even if everyone approved of them.
Morality is something people invented, like money.
I will pay more for something well made when a plain one would do.
Decoration is the first thing I would cut.

attachment.title: Social
attachment.tag: 25 questions · what kind of friend you are

questions.q: I show people I care without being asked.
I'm quick with a hug or a kind word.
Friends know I'll show up when it matters.
Once you're my friend, you're my friend for years.
I say what I'm feeling rather than keeping it in.
I let people see the messy parts of me.
I'm usually the one keeping things light and fun.
I'd rather joke around than be too serious.
Little gets under my skin in a friendship.
I give people room and don't keep score.
Showing affection doesn't come naturally to me.
My friendships tend to fade when life gets busy.
I keep my problems to myself.
I take most things seriously, even the small stuff.
I keep track of who reached out last.
I tell my friends what they mean to me.
Compliments feel awkward coming out of my mouth.
I still keep up with people I met years ago.
When someone moves away, we usually lose touch.
I will admit it when I am struggling.
There are things about me nobody in my life knows.
I am the one who suggests something daft.
I find it hard to switch off and mess about.
A friend cancelling on me barely registers.
It bothers me when a friend doesn't reply for days.

cognitive.title: Thinking
cognitive.tag: how you get to an answer · 20 questions · 4 modes

questions.q: I break a problem into pieces before I start on it.
I want the numbers in front of me before I take a view.
I check whether an argument actually follows.
I would rather go with a hunch than work it through.
I lose interest once a problem gets fiddly.
I look for the pattern before I look at the parts.
I want to know how a thing fits into everything around it.
When something breaks I look upstream for the cause.
I would rather fix what is in front of me than ask why it keeps happening.
Diagrams and maps rarely help me think.
I can tell when the mood in a room has shifted.
I work out what someone wants before they say it.
I think about how a decision will land on people.
Other people's reasons are mostly a mystery to me.
I judge an idea on its merits and leave the people out of it.
I understand something once I have built it myself.
I would rather try it than read about it.
I learn a tool by opening it and pressing things.
I want the instructions before I touch anything.
I would rather plan it properly than start and adjust.
